_comment: Curated TKE (Kubernetes worker node) risk overrides. Layered onto the generated catalog by generate_catalog.py. 'risk' levels: breaking = will stop node join or pod networking/runtime; caution = may affect some workloads or debugging; safe = default (no entry needed). 'lever' names the role variable that controls the safe behaviour. Derived from analysing the RHEL10-CIS role tasks.

3.3.1.1.reason: Disables net.ipv4.ip_forward. kube-proxy and every CNI require ip_forward=1 for pod/Service routing.

3.3.1.2.reason: Disables net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding. Breaks pod-to-pod and NodePort routing.

3.3.1.3.reason: Disables net.ipv4.conf.default.forwarding. Breaks forwarding on new interfaces (pod veths).

3.3.2.1.reason: Disables IPv6 all.forwarding. Only breaks IPv6/dual-stack clusters; harmless for IPv4-only.

3.3.2.2.reason: Disables IPv6 default.forwarding. Only relevant for IPv6/dual-stack clusters.

1.1.2.4.2.reason: Adds nodev to /var. kubelet/containerd operate under /var/lib; nodev is usually tolerable but relaxed to be safe.

1.1.2.4.3.reason: Adds nosuid to /var. Can affect some CSI/CNI helper binaries under /var/lib.

1.1.2.1.4.reason: Adds noexec to /tmp. Kubernetes does not exec from /tmp, but some bootstrap/Helm hooks might.

4.reason: firewalld with the default public zone blocks kubelet (10250), NodePort (30000-32767), and CNI overlay traffic. Nothing in the role opens these ports.
4.note: TKE worker nodes are fronted by a Tencent Security Group, which is the enforced network boundary.

rhel10cis_selinux_enforce.reason: SELinux enforcing may block containerd/kubelet without validated contexts (needs container-selinux).

rhel10cis_is_router.reason: Primary lever to keep IPv4+IPv6 forwarding on for kube-proxy/CNI.
